你在文具店挑了半天，最后买了一块小猫橡皮。回家舍不得擦，先摆在了铅笔盒正中间。: You spend ages choosing at the stationery shop and finally buy a little cat-shaped eraser. At home you can't bear to use it and set it right in the middle of your pencil case.
暴雨停了，路边还有积水。你和伙伴折了纸船，蹲在台阶上看它们漂远。: The downpour has stopped, but there's still water by the roadside. You and a friend fold paper boats and crouch on the steps watching them drift away.
夏天很长。你在旧书店的过道里翻了一下午书，老板送你一张褪了色的书签。: The summer is long. You spend a whole afternoon browsing in the aisles of a second-hand bookshop, and the owner gives you a faded bookmark.
晒床单的绳子不够长，你折腾了半天。邻居递来两个夹子，说夹住两头就不会掉。: The line for drying sheets isn't long enough, and you struggle with it for ages. A neighbour passes you two clips and says pinning both ends will keep it from falling.
你发现傍晚收摊前，青菜能便宜一块钱。卖菜的阿姨看你常来，添了一把葱。: You find that greens are one yuan cheaper just before the stalls close in the evening. Seeing you come often, the vegetable seller adds a bunch of spring onions.
你路过旧街，看见工人在补红砖墙。剥落的墙皮下面，露出一家早已关门的粮店招牌。: Passing through the old street, you see workers patching a red-brick wall. Beneath the peeling plaster appears the sign of a grain shop that closed long ago.
天闷得吃不下饭。你拌了一碗凉面，多放了醋，吃完又去切了半个西瓜。: It's too muggy to eat. You toss a bowl of cold noodles with extra vinegar, and afterwards cut half a watermelon.
社区的小球赛开了场。你在旁边看，隔壁卖早点的师傅打进一个好球，大家一起叫好。: A small neighbourhood ball game kicks off. You watch from the side, and the breakfast vendor from next door scores a great goal; everyone cheers.
你跟着看了一部家族故事剧。第二天买菜，摊主也在说昨晚那集，两个人争了半天谁有理。: You follow a family drama series. The next day at the market, the stallholder is talking about last night's episode too, and the two of you argue for ages over who was right.
你清出阳台的一角，搬来两盆万年青。浇水时发现楼下的猫也在仰着头晒太阳。: You clear a corner of the balcony and bring in two evergreen plants. While watering them you notice the cat downstairs is also tilting its head up to bask in the sun.
冬至，邻居端来一小碗饺子。你回送了一碟腌萝卜，两个空碗在楼道里换了回来。: On the winter solstice, a neighbour brings a small bowl of dumplings. You send back a dish of pickled radish, and the two empty bowls get swapped back in the stairwell.
连着下雨，小区门口积了水。有人搬来几块砖，摆成一条歪歪的路，后来又添了一根扶手。: It rains for days and water pools at the compound gate. Someone brings a few bricks and lays a crooked path, and later a handrail is added.
你在旧书摊买了一本生活杂志。封面上说流行的衣服，跟你柜子里压了多年的一件很像。: You buy a lifestyle magazine at a second-hand stall. The fashionable clothes on the cover look a lot like one that's been sitting at the bottom of your wardrobe for years.
春笋比去年贵了两块钱。你挑了两根，回家剥了一盆壳，锅里最后只剩小小一盘。: Spring bamboo shoots cost two yuan more than last year. You pick two, peel a whole basin of husks at home, and end up with only a small plate in the pot.
社区办了一场邻里晚会。有人唱跑了调，台下笑着鼓掌，凳子不够坐就从家里搬。: The neighbourhood holds an evening party. Someone sings off-key, the audience laughs and applauds, and when there aren't enough seats people bring stools from home.
你买了一小包新茶。第一次水放得太烫，第二次慢慢等，终于喝出一点回甜。: You buy a small pack of new tea. The first time the water is too hot; the second time you wait patiently and finally taste a hint of sweetness.
中秋晚上，你在窗边剥核桃。隔壁传来猜灯谜的笑声，你也猜出了一个，没好意思喊。: On Mid-Autumn night, you sit at the window cracking walnuts. Laughter from next door guessing lantern riddles drifts over; you solve one too, but feel too shy to shout it out.
花鸟市场添了几家摊位。你问完一盆花的价钱，又站着听了一会儿鸟叫，最后只买了一包花: A few new stalls have opened at the flower and bird market. After asking the price of a potted flower, you stand a while listening to the birds, and end up buying only a packet of seeds.
你在社区活动室试着画竹子。第一笔水太多，晕成一团，老师说先留下，过阵子再来看。: At the community activity room you try painting bamboo. The first stroke has too much water and blurs into a blot; the teacher says to keep it and look again in a while.
你和老邻居在凉亭里避雨。聊到门口那排树刚种下时只有手腕粗，如今已经遮住了半条路。: You and an old neighbour shelter from the rain in a pavilion. You talk about how the row of trees by the gate was only as thick as a wrist when planted, and now shades half the road.
你把穿旧的鞋送去换底。修鞋的人说这双做得好，还能穿，顺手把松了的线也补上。: You take your worn shoes to have the soles replaced. The repairman says they're well made and still good to wear, and mends the loose stitching while he's at it.
立冬，你给自己煮了一锅热汤。窗玻璃蒙上一层水汽，锅盖轻轻响，屋里暖了起来。: On the first day of winter, you cook yourself a pot of hot soup. The window glass fogs over, the lid rattles softly, and the room warms up.
你坐在路边长椅上，看清早的菜场开门。卖豆腐的把白布揭开，热气一下散进了凉风里。: You sit on a roadside bench and watch the morning market open. The tofu seller lifts the white cloth, and the steam disperses at once into the cool breeze.
邻居帮你把一袋米提进门。你从柜子里取出一包芝麻糖，让对方带回去，说别嫌少。: A neighbour helps carry a bag of rice into your home. You take a pack of sesame candy from the cupboard and press it on them, saying don't mind that it's so little.
你在楼下的小花园坐了一会儿。麻雀落下来啄草籽，有一只蹦到鞋边，又很快飞走。: You sit for a while in the small garden downstairs. Sparrows land to peck at grass seeds, and one hops up beside your shoe before quickly flying off.
天晴了，你把旧毛衣摊在窗边。阳光照着细细的绒毛，你认出袖口那处补过的针脚。: The weather clears, and you spread an old sweater by the window. Sunlight falls on the fine fuzz, and you recognise the darned stitches at the cuff.
清早一束光落在被角上。你伸手摸了摸，还是凉的，便又慢慢把手缩回被窝。: Early in the morning a shaft of light falls on the corner of the quilt. You reach out and touch it, still cool, and slowly pull your hand back under the covers.
窗外有风吹过树叶。你坐着听了一会儿，远处有人叫卖，声音跟很多年前一样。: Wind passes through the leaves outside the window. You sit and listen for a while; far off someone is hawking goods, in a voice just like many years ago.
你翻出一叠旧信。有几个字已经认不清，信纸里夹着的那片叶子，却还留着细细的叶脉。: You dig out a bundle of old letters. Some of the words are no longer legible, but the leaf pressed between the pages still shows its fine veins.
大年初一，楼道里有人互相道好。你把门口的红纸抚平，听见有个孩子在数收到的糖。: On the first day of the New Year, people in the stairwell exchange greetings. You smooth the red paper at your door and hear a child counting the sweets he's been given.
年节集市重新摆到了河边，捏面人的摊子前排着长队。: The festival market is set up again by the river, with a long queue in front of the dough-figurine stall.
这个夏天热得早，街边的绿豆汤摊比往年提前开了门。: This summer got hot early, and the mung-bean soup stalls on the street opened earlier than usual.
菜价连涨了几周，晚市里问完价再买的人多了。: Vegetable prices have risen for several weeks, and more people at the evening market ask the price before buying.
一部短剧热播，街坊碰面先问对方看到了第几集。: A short drama series is a hit, and when neighbours meet they first ask which episode the other has reached.
不少老小区修好了漏雨的屋顶，楼道里晒满了搬出来的旧被子。: Many old compounds have had their leaking roofs repaired, and the stairwells are full of old quilts hung out to air.
地方联赛决赛那天，好些小饭馆把桌子并到一起，边吃边看球。: On the day of the local league final, many small restaurants push their tables together so people can eat while watching the match.
城里添了几处口袋公园，午后歇脚终于不用总找商场。: The city has added several pocket parks, so you no longer always need a mall to rest in the afternoon.
今年中秋晴得好，月饼摊主收摊后，也搬了凳子坐到门口。: The weather is clear this Mid-Autumn, and after packing up, the mooncake stallholders bring stools out to sit at their doors.
你想起小时候那次视频电话，后来安排回家时，也会先问清彼此有空的日子。: You remember that video call from childhood, and when later arranging trips home, you first ask which days each of you is free.
小时候在小卖部写作业的那张桌子，你还记得，谈起做生意的辛苦，也会多听几句。: You still remember the table where you did homework in the little shop as a child, and when people talk about how hard running a business is, you listen a bit longer.
小时候免费托管班的那本练习册，你还记得，碰到拿不准的题，也愿意开口问人。: You still remember the workbook from the free after-school care as a child, and when you meet a question you're unsure of, you're willing to ask someone.
小时候练过的特长，后来未必成了职业，认真练过一遍的感觉却还在。: The skill you practised as a child may not have become a career, but the feeling of having practised it seriously is still with you.
你想起那位转学同学，课间一起跳房子、互教老家话的事，仍然记得。: You think of that transfer student, and still remember playing hopscotch together at break and teaching each other your hometown dialects.
你翻到那位转学同学当年寄来的高中照片，想起两个人互教老家话的课间，近况已经不清楚: You come across the high school photo that transfer student sent you back then, and recall the breaks spent teaching each other your hometown dialects. You no longer know how they are now, but the photo is still kept.
收拾旧物时，你又看见转学同学当年发来的照片，想起那几节一起跳房子的课间。: Tidying old things, you see again the photo that transfer student sent, and remember those breaks playing hopscotch together.
你想起第一次学厨切坏的那些土豆，师傅当年多盛的那碗饭，到现在还记得。: You think of the potatoes you ruined cutting when you first learned to cook, and still remember the extra bowl of rice the master served you back then.
工作遇到难处，你想起学厨时挨过的那顿数落，也想起师傅收工后多盛的那碗饭。: When work gets hard, you recall the scolding you got while learning to cook, and also the extra bowl of rice the master served after closing.
你想起当年跟着村里叔叔走过的巷子，工具箱怎么摆，至今还照着最早学的习惯。: You remember the alleys you walked behind the village uncle back then; to this day you still arrange your toolbox the way you first learned.
整理工具时，你想起当年跟村里叔叔学手艺的日子，那些活做慢一点也得核清楚。: Sorting your tools, you recall the days learning the trade from the village uncle, when even slow work had to be checked clearly.
小时候家里的钱要算着花，这些年有事商量，你也习惯先把眼前能承担的说清楚。: As a child your family had to count every coin, and these years when discussing things, you also make a habit of stating first what you can afford right now.
小时候家里替你安排过不少事，如今自己的日子怎么过，还得一件件拿主意。: Your family arranged many things for you as a child, and now you have to decide how to live your own days, one thing at a time.
小时候看惯了大人按点上下班，如今家里的时间表，轮到你自己慢慢排。: As a child you were used to adults going to and from work on the dot, and now it's your turn to arrange the household schedule slowly yourself.
小时候见过家里忙进忙出，如今算日常的账，也会给做不完的事留一点余地。: As a child you saw your family bustling in and out, and now when you do the daily accounts, you leave a little room for the things that can't all get done.

一碗面端上桌时的香气: the aroma of a bowl of noodles set on the table
